Title: Use every supplied occurrence
Rule: A valid Game24 expression uses every supplied number occurrence exactly once.
A repeated numeric value represents repeated occurrences; multiplicity must be preserved.

Title: Allowed operations
Rule: Use only addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division between supplied values or their intermediate results.
Do not use concatenation, exponentiation, factorials, or newly introduced numeric constants.

Title: Parenthesization
Rule: Parentheses may determine the order of arithmetic evaluation.
The validity of the expression is determined by its exact arithmetic structure, not by a bag of operations.

Title: Exact target
Rule: The final value of the complete expression must be exactly 24 under exact arithmetic.
An expression that is merely close to 24 is incorrect.

Title: Intermediate values
Rule: Negative and fractional intermediate values are allowed when they arise from the permitted operations.
Division by zero is never allowed.

Title: No hidden number reuse
Rule: A subexpression cannot reuse a supplied number occurrence that has already been consumed elsewhere in the expression.
The complete expression must account for the original multiset exactly.

Title: Duplicate numbers
Rule: When the input contains duplicate values, treat them as distinct occurrences with the stated multiplicity.
Using one occurrence twice is invalid even when the repeated values are numerically identical.

Title: Division by zero
Rule: Any expression tree containing division by an intermediate value equal to zero is invalid regardless of its other branches.

Title: Noncommutative operations
Rule: Subtraction and division are order-sensitive.
Swapping their left and right operands can change both the intermediate value and final validity.

Title: Fractional paths
Rule: Do not reject a candidate merely because an intermediate result is fractional.
A fractional path is valid if every operation is defined and the complete exact value is 24.

Title: Correct value with wrong multiplicity
Rule: Reaching 24 is insufficient when a supplied occurrence is omitted, duplicated, or replaced.
Both arithmetic equality and exact occurrence use are required.

Title: Syntactic shortcuts
Rule: A notation that implicitly concatenates digits or introduces an operation outside the registered four operators does not satisfy the Game24 task even if its numerical value is 24.

Title: Factor the target
Rule: A useful search strategy is to look for intermediate factors of 24, such as 2 and 12, 3 and 8, or 4 and 6, and test whether disjoint subsets of the supplied occurrences can produce them.

Title: Pair subexpressions
Rule: Partitioning the four occurrences into small subexpressions can reduce search complexity.
After constructing each subexpression, combine them only if their occurrence sets are disjoint.

Title: Create a small adjustment
Rule: Differences or ratios that produce a small adjustment such as 1 can help convert another intermediate value into 24.
Always verify that the adjustment itself uses only unused supplied occurrences.

Title: Check subtraction routes
Rule: When direct multiplication overshoots the target, test whether a remaining subexpression can be subtracted to reach 24.

Title: Preserve exact divisibility when useful
Rule: When considering division, prefer branches whose denominator is nonzero and whose resulting exact value can still combine naturally with the remaining occurrences.
This is a search heuristic, not a validity requirement.

Title: Final audit
Rule: Before accepting a candidate, audit both conditions independently: every supplied occurrence appears exactly once, and exact evaluation of the complete expression equals 24.
